title: 2016 AMC 12B Problem 23

concepts.label: Power scaling of length, area, and volume

statement: What is the volume of the region in three-dimensional space defined by the inequalities \(|x|+|y|+|z|\le1\) and \(|x|+|y|+|z-1|\le1?\)

solutions.text:
The region \(|x|+|y|+|z|\le1\) is a regular octahedron with vertices at \((\pm1,0,0),(0,\pm1,0),(0,0,\pm1),\) whose volume is \(2\cdot\tfrac13\cdot(\sqrt2)^2\cdot1=\tfrac43.\) The second region is the same octahedron shifted up by \(1.\) Their intersection is bounded by another regular octahedron with diagonals of length \(1,\) half the linear dimensions of the first, so its volume is \(\left(\tfrac12\right)^3\cdot\tfrac43=\tfrac16.\)

Thus, the correct answer is A.
hints: The set \(|x|+|y|+|z|\le1\) is a regular octahedron with diagonals of length \(2\) and volume \(\tfrac43\)
The second inequality is that octahedron translated up by \(1;\) their overlap is a similar octahedron with half the linear size
